function: ISAC channel, power and bandwidth allocation by DDPG/DQN over scalar single-antenna links without RIS; p. 3: "stands for the downlink channel gain for vehicle k on the subchannel j"
notes: Excluded at code 6 (system). Codes 1-5 pass: research article; DDPG learns subchannel and transmit power, p. 6: "defined as a binary tuple" (subchannel, power), and DQN learns the sensing/communication bandwidth split under a sensing-rate threshold (pp. 4, 6-7), i.e. resources serving sensing and communication, so area 5 and physical layer (power is learned jointly with the subchannel choice). The link model is single-antenna with no RIS: the SINR (1) uses a scalar gain, p. 3: "stands for the downlink channel gain for vehicle k on the subchannel j"; p. 4: "G denotes the transmit antenna gain of the BS; Gr,c is the receive antenna gain of a vehicle"; p. 7, Table II (read as image): "Tx antenna gain G" 30 dB, "Communication Rx antenna gain" 0 dB. No antenna count, array, beamforming, or MIMO appears anywhere; terrestrial V2X at 2 GHz, not OTFS or NTN, so the single-antenna exception does not apply.
